about.hero_lead: An open knowledge graph linking EU companies, public procurement, lobbyists and cohesion funding.
about.mission_body_1: Public debate runs on numbers — budgets and contracts, migration and emissions, who owns what, even the text of a law — and they are constantly bent to fit an argument. Fontem links the primary sources behind those claims into one open, cross-checked graph, so a claim can be followed back to the evidence instead of taken on trust.
about.mission_body_2: That is the groundwork, not the goal. Misleading claims thrive when checking them is hard work; we make it a click. And a public that can verify what it is told can take a real part in what comes next — so Fontem surfaces, in context, the concrete ways to do exactly that.
about.mission_lead: We are building the civic layer for European democracy — where any public claim can be traced back to the numbers behind it.
about.step_crosscheck_desc: Compare what TED, GLEIF, the Transparency Register, Cohesion and other sources say about the same entity, side by side.
about.step_crosscheck_gif_alt: Switching between procurement, financial and lobbying views
about.step_publish_desc: Write up what you find as a data story and publish it — private, signed-in only, or fully public.
about.step_publish_gif_alt: Publishing a data story from the editor
about.step_search_desc: Look up any company, contracting authority, lobbyist or EU-funded project by name or identifier.
about.step_search_gif_alt: Searching for an entity in Fontem
about.value_open_desc: The graph, the methods and the code behind it are public.
about.value_participation_desc: Checking the facts is the means, not the goal. An informed, engaged public is.
about.value_sourced_desc: Every figure links back to the official register it came from. We connect the data; we do not editorialise it.
about.walkthrough_searching_a_company_explorin: Walkthrough: searching a company, exploring procurement, and publishing a data story

data_quality.concern_concession_negative: Negative (concession) value; excluded from value totals.
data_quality.concern_implausible_magnitude: Value too large to be plausible for a single contract; excluded from totals.
data_quality.concern_low_confidence: Low-confidence value; excluded from totals pending review.
data_quality.concern_payable_discrepancy: The source listed a conflicting payable amount (possible data-entry error such as a ×1000 inflation).
data_quality.concern_unverified: Value could not be cross-checked against an estimate.
data_quality.concern_value_disagreement: Awarded value disagrees with the budget estimate; excluded from totals.
data_quality.failed_to_load_data_quality_metrics: Failed to load data quality metrics.
data_quality.platform_health_data_coverage_and_transp: Platform health, data coverage, and transparency metrics
data_quality.withheld_audit_note: The published number was removed from the platform because it failed hard sanity checks. The original claim is preserved in the audit log and the review queue; if a reviewer establishes the true value it will appear here.
data_quality.explain_implausible_magnitude: The published value is orders of magnitude beyond any plausible public contract — usually a currency or price-per-unit error in the source notice.
data_quality.explain_concession_negative: The notice published a negative value — an accounting artifact of how the form was filled in, not a price.
data_quality.explain_unverified: Only one uncorroborated money field was published, at a magnitude that made it suspect, with nothing to cross-check it against.
data_quality.explain_zero_value: The notice published a value of exactly zero — non-disclosure wearing a number. Treated as an undisclosed value.
data_quality.explain_confirmed_bogus: A human reviewer examined the published value and confirmed it is unreliable. No trustworthy value is available for this contract.
data_quality.explain_withheld_generic: The published value failed the platform's sanity checks and was withheld.
data_quality.explain_low_confidence_generic: The value is shown, but the published money fields are weakly evidenced; it is excluded from default totals and rankings.

help.title: Help
help.connect_intro: Fontem exposes its data as tools your own AI client can call — company records, contracts, the entity graph, SPARQL. You use the assistant you already pay for, and Fontem never sees your provider account.
help.step_token_body_post: → {section} → {action}. Copy it immediately: it is shown once and cannot be retrieved afterwards. If you lose it, revoke it and make another.
help.claude_desktop_body: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Paste the URL above, and your token as the bearer token.
help.chatgpt_body: Settings → Connectors → Add. ChatGPT's connector support requires a paid plan; the URL and token are the same.
help.anything_else_body: Any client speaking MCP over Streamable HTTP works. Send the token as {header}.
help.step_ask_body: Try {example}. Your client decides when to call Fontem's tools.
help.step_ask_example: “Use Fontem to find contracts awarded to companies linked to X”
help.revoking_body: Account settings lists every connected client with when it was last used. Revoking takes effect on the next request. If you no longer recognise a client, revoke it.
help.why_key_title: Why do I need my own AI account?
help.why_key_body_1: Because no AI provider sells what would otherwise be the obvious arrangement. Anthropic prohibited using a Claude subscription inside third-party tools in February 2026 and blocked it that April; OpenAI's ChatGPT plans have never included API access; and Mistral bills Le Chat and its API separately. A site like Fontem genuinely cannot spend your subscription on your behalf.
help.why_key_body_2: What it can do is hand your own assistant the data. That is better than the alternative, not merely cheaper for us: you keep your provider, your history and your privacy settings, you are not rationed by a budget we set, and nothing breaks here when a vendor changes its terms.
help.in_app_body_1: There is also an assistant built into the site, on every page. It can search the data, explain what you are looking at, move you around the platform, and — while you are editing an article — propose changes to it.
help.in_app_body_2_pre: It needs an API key from Anthropic, Mistral or OpenAI, added in
help.in_app_body_2_post: . That is pay-per-use and typically costs very little; a subscription is not required and would not work here anyway, for the reasons above.
help.privacy_item_page: The page you are on, and the list of pages it can take you to.
help.privacy_item_data: The public data it looks up on your behalf.
help.privacy_item_article: The article you are editing, while you are editing it.
help.privacy_body_1: It cannot see other people's private drafts, and it is offered only the tools that make sense where you are — it cannot propose edits when no article is open.
help.privacy_body_2: Your provider key is stored encrypted and is never shown again after you save it. Tokens for external clients are stored only as a hash, so they cannot be recovered from our database — which is why a new one is shown exactly once.

provider_keys.title: Assistant provider
provider_keys.intro: The assistant runs on Fontem's own built-in model by default — nothing to configure. You can point it at your own LLM account instead if you want a larger model; keys are stored encrypted and are never shown again after saving.
provider_keys.empty: No provider configured — the assistant is unavailable until you add one.
provider_keys.saved_notice: Key saved. The assistant will use it from your next message.
provider_keys.builtin_note: Runs on Fontem's own hardware. No account, no key, nothing billed to you. It is a small model, so it is slower and less capable than a paid one — but it needs nothing from you to work.
provider_keys.builtin_superseded: Your own key is being used instead. Remove it to go back to the built-in model.
provider_keys.byo_intro: Optional. A key from Anthropic, Mistral or OpenAI gets you a larger, faster model, billed to you by them.
